txt: The present study examined the effects of a 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) 6 receptor antagonist, Ro 04-6790, on novel object recognition and trace conditioning in adult male Wistar rats. The present study used a novel test of novel object exploration to detect enhanced recognition memory under Ro 04–6790. The procedure used was based on the use of a 30 s interval between sample and test stages of the procedure, which provided a suitable baseline from which to detect novel object discrimination. The specific doses of Ro 04‐6790 examined were those previously found to enhance recognition memory tested after a 4 h delay. The effects of Ro‐67‐90 were compared in a trace conditioning procedure which holds promise as a behavioral assay for hippocampus-dependent working memory function, as well as in the standard test of object recognition memory. The rats were trained to recognize two identical copies of the same object in the same arena. The animals were then tested for novel object identification in the absence of a background stimulus. The results showed that Ro‐68‐90 did not affect the ability to discriminate between the two objects. However, the rats did exhibit a significant increase in novel object discovery when the background stimulus was present. The effect of Ro-68‐990 on trace conditioning was similar to that of the 5-HT6 antagonist, suggesting that the novel object-recognition test may be a useful tool for investigating the neurobiological substrates of recognition memory in animals.

txt: The serotonergic system is involved in a variety of cognitive and behavioral processes, including various aspects of learning and memory. The recently identified 5-HT6 receptor has been a particular target for cognitive enhancers. The present study examined the effects of the 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT)6 receptor antagonist Ro 04-6790 on the ability to discriminate between novel and familiar objects in a novel object recognition apparatus. The rats were trained to discriminate novel and known objects in the arena, and then tested for enhanced recognition memory over a 30 s interval suitable to detect enhanced conditioning. Ro 04–6790 did not improve recognition memory. However, it decreased object exploration at 10 mg/kg. The novel object exploration was not affected by the presence of a background stimulus, suggesting that the novel object was not better associated than the familiar object. The results suggest that the 5‐HT6 antagonist does not improve memory of recognition memory, but does decrease object exploration.

txt: The present study investigated the effects of 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT6) receptor antagonist Ro 04-6790 on trace conditioning and object recognition memory in adult male Wistar rats. The present procedure was used to establish baseline conditioning and to test novel object recognition. The procedure was adapted to include an experimental background stimulus to measure contextual object recognition and to measure object exploration. The specific doses of Ro 04–6790 examined were those previously found to enhance recognition memory tested after a 4 h delay. The results of the present study show that Ro 04‐6790 does not improve recognition memory at doses previously found previously to enhance memory function. However, it does increase trace conditioning, a profile consistent with increased selectivity. The indirect catecholamine agonists d-amphetamine and methylphenidate both increased associative learning to both trace conditioned and contextual cues, a pattern consistent with reduced selectivity, whereas the neurotensin agonist PD 149163 selectively increased trace conditioning but did not affect conditioning at 0 s interval between CS and UCS, and reduced conditioning to box context. Ro 04−6790 did not improve trace conditioning or contextual conditioning. Additionally, Ro 04 −6790 decreased object exploration at 10 mg/kg.

txt: Cytochrome P450 2E1 T303A, a mutant of cytochrome-P450 2e1 in which the highly conserved threonine in the I-helix (Thr252) was mutated to alanine, has been used to investigate the role of this highly conservized threonines in catalysis. This mutant showed higher catalytic activities for several substrates in comparison to the wild type enzyme. We have previously investigated the role that T303 plays in the inactivation of P4502E1 by mechanism-based inactivators. Here, we have shown that an accelerated auto-inactivation of 2E2E2A mutant occurs during incubation with reductase, even in the absence of inactivator. This auto-activation could be prevented by co-incubation with catalase. Interestingly, this accelerated inactivation during catalytic turnover was also found with the 2B4 T302A mutant, which corresponds to 2E3A. Our present results suggest that the conserved T303 residue might stabilize the P450 or decrease production of a reactive heme-oxygen intermediate to prevent the accelerated autoinactivation which can occur in the presence of hydrogen peroxide during electron transfer from the reductases under aerobic conditions. We propose here a novel concept for the role for this highly highly conservated threoninine and an explanation of why P450s may require this highly-conserved residue in the active site.

txt: The highly conserved threonine residue in the I-helix of cytochrome P450 2E1 T303A has been implicated as playing a role in dioxygen activation during catalytic turnover. This highly conservized threonines has been a target of mutation studies in bacterial (P450cam, P450BM3) and mammalian (PODAC, PODAC2) P450s. The results of these studies suggested that this threonin-252 residue may be associated with diooxygen stabilization, proton delivery, and substrate recognition. However, it has been surprising that some mutants where the threonino-threonine was replaced with an aliphatic residue exhibit significant catalytic activities and/or NADPH consumption rates when compared to the wild type enzymes. In this study, we investigated the role of the highly conservated threoninate in the active site of P4502E1 and the T303 mutant in the absence of inactivators. We found that the T3A mutant of PODACE exhibited an accelerated auto-inactivation during incubation with reductase, even in the presence of inactivation by reductases. This auto-activation was accompanied by heme destruction and part of the heme became covalently attached to the apoprotein. Interestingly, this accelerated inactivation during catalytically turnover was also found with the 2B4 T302A mutant, which corresponds to 2E2E2T303A. Our present results suggest that the highly highly conserving threoninedependent threonidine might stabilize the P450 or decrease production of a reactive heme-oxygen intermediate to prevent the accelerated autoinactivation which can occur in the environment of hydrogen peroxide during catalyzed electron transfer from the reduct enzyme under aerobic conditions.

txt: Cytochrome P450s are highly conserved monooxygenases that are involved in steroid biosynthesis, drug metabolism, and detoxification of xenobiotics. A threonine residue in the I-helix (Thr252) in the distal side of the heme is one of the most highly conservated residues in the P450 family. We have previously investigated the role that T303 plays in the inactivation of wild-type P450 2E1 and the T303A mutant by mechanism-based inactivators. We now report that an accelerated auto-inactivation of 2E-T303A was observed during incubation with reductase, even in the absence of inactivator. As presented here, this auto-Inactivation of the mutant was much faster than that seen with the wild-typical enzyme and could be prevented by co-incubation with catalase. The auto-induction of auto-activation was accompanied by heme destruction and part of the hemeproteins became covalently attached to the apoprotein. Interestingly, this accelerated autoinactivation during catalytic turnover was also found with the 2B4 T302A mutant, which corresponds to 2E 1 T303 A. Our present results suggest that the highly conservized threonines may stabilize the P-helical structure or decrease production of a reactive heme-oxygen intermediate to prevent the accelerated autoactivation which can occur in the presence of hydrogen peroxide during electron transfer from the reductases under aerobic conditions. We propose here a novel concept for the role of this highly conservised threoninine and an explanation of why P450 enzymes may require this highly highly conservared threoninoamine residue in their active site.

txt: The effects of intracellular mechanical force on endothelial cells are poorly understood. We studied the effects of magnetic force on Human Umbilical Vein Endothelial Cells (Huvec) and its potential applications. The subcellular location of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIOs) was verified. Cell responses on the cellular and subcellulo levels, including intracecellular relocalization and cell migration, were observed and discussed. The results suggest that the force exerted on the inside surface of the cell membrane guided and accelerated cell migration. The force exerted inside the cell was localized to the cell nucleus and the migration direction was the same as the force direction. The cytoskeleton of the cells sensed the force generated inside the cells and maintained the mechanical structure of the cytoskeletal system. The magnetic force generated by magnetic force was localized in the lysosomes and lyso-lysosomes, which were taken up by cells via cell endocytosis. The intracellular localization of SPIOs was controlled by magnetic field gradient. The effect of magnetic field on cell migration was also studied. The migration direction of SPio-containing cells was the direction of the magnetic force. The potential applications of magnetic nanoparticles in cytomechanics and cell patterning are discussed.

txt: The effects of intracellular force on Human Umbilical Vein Endothelial Cells (Huvec) were studied. Magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) were coated with DSPE-PEG2000 and used to study the effects of a magnetic force on intracellular forces on Huvec. The subcellular location of SPIOs was verified. The effect of SPIOS on the cellular and subcellulo levels, including intracecellular relocalization and cell migration, was studied. The results show that the force exerted on SPIO inside cells is similar to that exerted on the outside surface of the cell membrane, which is similar with the effect of sheer flow. The force exerted inside the cell is more localized and can guide cell migration in a specific direction. The magnetic force can be used to control the movement of attached cells and to study cell patterning. The ability to control cell migration with a localized force is a self-defense mechanism to maintain the mechanical structure of the cells as a system. The potential applications of MNPs in cytomechanics and cell patterners are discussed.

txt: Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and guanosine tri-phosphates (GTP) are endogenous substrates that are utilized by numerous enzymes for their functions in the cell. In this study, we have investigated the molecular mechanisms that underlie the ATP and GTP selectivity of human adenylate kinase isoform 3 (AK3), a member of the nucleotide monophosphate kinases (NMP) family. We have determined the structure of AK3 and performed molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the molecular basis for the GTP versus ATP selectivity. We find that the ATP binding domain of AK-3 is highly flexible and flexible enough to accommodate a variety of substrates. The protein is able to discriminate between ATP and guanine tripsheets (GPs) with a Kd of 0.5 \xce\xbcM. The GTP binding domain is highly stable and does not undergo a large-scale conformational change upon ATP binding. The ATP binding site is stabilized by a hydrogen bond between the N6 of the adenine base and the backbone carbonyl oxygen of Lys200. The binding of GTP to the ATP-binding site is weak and does so by a cation-\xcf\x80 (or stacking) interaction between the sidechain of Arg119 and the aromatic system of the aromatic base. The cationic sensing of the substrate is conserved for NMP kinases and is responsible for the 60-fold difference in catalytic activity between ATP (AKeco) and GPs. The molecular mechanisms of AKeco that governs the selectivity between ATP versus GTP are also conserved in human adenosine monophosphate kinas.

txt: Enzymes are responsible for the recognition of endogenous substrates in the crowded cellular milieu. To overcome this challenge, enzymes can employ positive and negative selection mechanisms to recruit and reject substrates respectively, both of which require evolution of distinct molecular mechanisms. A particular example is the ability of enzymes to discriminate between adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and guanosine tri-phosphates (GTP) and to use these substrates as phosphoryl donors. Here, we have studied two monomeric and long nucleotide monophosphate kinases, AK3 and AKeco, which are members of the nucleotide triphphosphatase family. We have discovered that the GTP selectivity of AKeco is governed by a cation-\xcf\x80 (or stacking) interaction between the sidechain of Arg119 and the aromatic system of the adenine base. The GTP versus ATP selectivity is conserved in other nucleotide kinases. In AKeco the nucleation of an induced fit transition by ATP is nucleated by formation of a covalent interaction between Arg119 of the ATP binding domain and the side chain of the aromatic side chain. In contrast, the GFP-binding domain of AK3 is nucleation by formation a cobalonyl-hydrogen bond between the backbone carbonyl oxygen of Lys200 and the N6 of the amino acid. The molecular mechanisms that underlie the GMP-mediated ATP recognition of AKeco are also conserved for other nucleotides. In addition, we find that protein surfaces offer a general and weak affinity for both GTP and ATP.

txt: The human mitochondrial adenylate kinase AK3 is a member of the nucleotide monophosphate (NMP) kinase family. The enzyme is a monomeric and long NMP kinase that is expressed in the human mitochondrial matrix and its role is to shuttle adenosine triphosphate into GDP as GDP is used by succinyl-CoA synthetase in the citric acid (TCA) cycle. Through an integrative structural biology approach combining X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations, we reveal the molecular mechanisms that underlie the GTP selectivity of AK3. In addition and by examining observations off non-linearity of chemical shifts in GTP and ATP titrations, we find that protein surfaces offer a general and weak affinity for both GTP (Kd = 0.5 \xce\xbcM) and ATP (Ki = 0 \xcf\x83).

txt: Background2-Amino-6-chloropyridine (AMPY) is a widely used pharmaceutical ingredient. It is a derivative of 2-aminopyridinium (2ABA) and 2-amino-6chloropyrimidine (2AMPY). The aim of this study was to prepare and characterize the co-crystals of AMPY with benzoic acid derivatives.ResultsThe co-cations of AMYP with benzosic acid and its derivatives were prepared and characterized by 1H NMR, 13CNMR, IR, TEM analysis and XRD. The co-incubations of 2ABA and its derivative, 3-chlorobenzoic (3CLBA) were prepared by the reaction of hot methanol solution of AMPH with the corresponding benzoate derivatives. The XRD data of (II-V) were obtained. The crystal structures of (I-V), (II), (III), (IV) and (V), were determined using single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The purity of the solid phase of these complexes was characterized by XRPD. The structures of the cocrystals were analyzed by IR spectroscopy, 1HNMR, photoluminescence, TGA and XRDS.ConclusionsThe cocrystal of AMMP with benzoyl acid derivatives was prepared and its crystal structures were determined. The supramolecular architectures of the compounds were studied by using common analytical tools such as 1H-NMR and 13CN-MR, TGE and XRF. The results of this investigation are of interest for the design of new pharmaceuticals.

txt: Background2-Amino-6-chloropyridine (AMPY) is a promising co-crystal material for the synthesis of pharmaceuticals. The aim of this study was to prepare and characterize the supramolecular architectures of four co-cations of benzoic acid derivatives (BA, 2ABA, 3CLBA and 4-NBA) with 2-amino-6chloropyrimidine (AMPY) (I) and to investigate the hydrogen-bonding patterns of the supra- and di-carboxylate moieties.ResultsThe crystal structures of (I-V) have been determined using single-crycrystal X-ray diffraction. The crystal structures were characterized by 1H NMR, 13CNMR, IR, photoluminescence, TEM analysis and XRD. The hydrogen-dependence of the crystal structures was studied by using 1HNMR, 1H-NMR and 13CN-NIR spectroscopy. The co-incubation of benzosic acid and its derivatives (II-V), with AMPY, formed the following supramoles: AMPYPY…BA (II), AMPYDBA (III), AMMPY…2ABA (IV) and AMPDPBA…3CLBA (V). The cocrystals were characterized using 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopic techniques.ConclusionsThe supramolcular architectures were characterized in the crystal structure of (II)-(V. It was observed that homosynthon was presented in crystal structure (I), whereas carboxylic acid…pyridine heterosynths were formed in all four cocrystal structures (II–(V). DADA arrays were observed in the co-stal structures of compound (IV). These DADA array of hydrogen-linked motifs have been observed in many 2,4-diaminopyrimidines.Graphical abstractThree types of supramolycular synthons, (A), (B) and (C), were discussed in this paper.

txt: Arctic ground squirrels (AGS, Spermophilus parryii) are an extreme heterothermic endotherm and experience the most severe overwinter environment (< \xe2\x88\x9220 \xc2\xb0C), the longest hibernation season (7\xe2*x80\x938 months), and consequently the shortest active season of any hibernator. We have recently demonstrated that euthermic AGS have low blood oxygen partial pressure (PaO2) and hemoglobin oxygen saturation (sO2), thus indicating a natural state of mild, chronic hypoxia. These observations suggest that AGS experience and tolerate chronic endogenous hypoxial during euthermy, and hypoxa may serve to precondition these animals for neuroprotection. In contrast to the PaO2 data in eutheric AGS, brain tissue oxygen partial pressures (PtO2, PaO 2) in winter interbout eutheracental AGS is normal and is higher than that in hibernating AGS. To our knowledge, there have been no investigations that demonstrate 1) the difference between PtO2 and PaOoflood in summer eutheriac AGS; 2) differences in PtOoflate and Paoflate between AGS and rats; 3) how brain tissue Oxygenation responds to environmental hypoxiative hypoxiation in AGS under exposure to hypoxic conditions. The present investigation was conducted to address these issues at physiological levels using in vivo measurements of brain tissue O2 in non-sedated and non-anesthetized, free-moving animals. We hypothesized that 1) PtOofthe brain tissue PtOfthe oxygen partialpressure (PdO2 of summer euthmic AGGSS differs from PaOofthetic and is high than that of rats; 2), PtOnthe brain oxygen partialpf (PtiO2" and Paofthe hemoglobin (pH) in AGGess are lower than that observed in rats; and 3) PtPtoprO2 is higher in AGSG than in rats. The results of the present investigation were compared with those of non-hibernating species. The data suggest that the heterotherm is distinct in hypoxic tolerance from non-heterotherms and that the state of the hetero-state is profoundly different from euthermia.

txt: Arctic ground squirrels (AGS) experience chronic endogenous hypoxia during euthermy, and hypoxial may serve to precondition these animals for neuroprotection. We hypothesized that 1) brain tissue oxygen partial pressure (PtO2) of summer euthermic AGS differs from PaO2 and is higher than that of rats; 2) PtO2 in AGS and PaO22 in AGSG respond to and tolerate environmental hypoxiosis differently from non-hibernating species in that AGS have better adaptive mechanisms to preserve functions during hypoxiation; and 3) AGS experience and tolerate chronic endogenous oxygenation during euterymy, but not hibernation. The present investigation was conducted to address those issues at physiological levels using in vivo measurements of brain tissue Oxygen Percentage Oxygen (PtiO2), PaO32, and pH in non-sedated and non-anesthetized, free-moving animals. We found that PtO32 and Pa32 in summer euteremic AGSG are higher than those in summer non-euthermic rats, and that both are higher in AGGS than in rats. In addition, PtO42 and Pa42 in AGGS are higher, as compared with rats, in the absence of hypoxias. In AGS, Pt and Pa22 are higher during eutermy than during hibernation, and both are lower than in AGGs during hibernating season. In contrast to AGSG, no differences in PtO22 and Pa46 were observed in AGSF during hypoxic gas exposure. These data suggest that AGSG experience and can tolerate chronic, endogenous hypoxic stress during euthmy, which may serve as a preconditional state for neuroprotective mechanisms.

txt: Arctic ground squirrels (AGS) are the most severe endotherm in the world and experience the most extreme endotherms, and the most hypoxic overwinter environment. We have recently demonstrated that AGS during hibernation are well oxygenated in blood, as compared with rats, and there is no evidence of cellular stress, inflammatory response, neuronal pathology, or oxidative modification following the period of high metabolic demand that is necessary for arousal. In contrast, euthermic AGS have low blood oxygen partial pressure (PaO2) and hemoglobin oxygen saturation (sO2), thus indicating a natural state of mild, chronic hypoxia. These observations suggest that AGG experience and tolerate chronic endogenous hypoxias during euthermy, and hypoxial may serve to precondition these animals for neuroprotection. To our knowledge, there have been no investigations that demonstrate 1) the difference between PtO2 and PaO2 in summer eutheric AGS; 2) differences in PtO 2 and Pa 2 between AGS and rats; and 3) how brain tissue oxygenation responds to environmental hypoxic conditions in AGS. The present investigation was conducted to address those issues at physiological levels using in vivo measurements of brain tissue Oxygenation (PtO2, PaO 2, and V\xcc\x87O2). We hypothesized that 1) PtO and Pa in summer-euthermic and non-hibernating AGS are higher than that in eutherics; 2), PtO in AGG and Pa of non-anesthetized rats are similar; and, 3) AGS experience and can tolerate environmental hypoxic conditions differently than non-Hibernators. We found that PtO, Pa, and oxygenation in AGSG are higher in summer than in winter-euthics, and that AGSG have better adaptive mechanisms to preserve functions during hypoxiation.

txt: The chemoselectivity of a reaction can be controlled by the relative rates of irreversible and reversible reactions. In a complex mixture of equilibrating precursors, this can be achieved by changing the rate of reagent addition. The key to this behavior is the use of coupled equilibria, in which the products of one reversible reaction act as the substrates for another. We show that this behavior can be exploited in dynamic combinatorial libraries (DCLs) to select products from a variety of its members, ranging from electron-rich to electron-poor. This product selection was accomplished in the absence of any enzyme or synthetic catalysts that could impart selectivity, and the only parameter changed was the rate at which reagent reagent additions were performed. These results may offer insights into processes in prebiotic chemistry.

txt: Control of chemoselectivity is among the central problems of synthetic chemistry. Often, reaction outcome is controlled by thermodynamic and kinetic factors. In a complex mixture of equilibrating precursors, reaction products can express either their kinetic (fastest formed) or thermodynamic (most stable) products. Are these two extremes the only options? In this Communication, we show that they are not: in a complex mixtures of reversible reactions, final reaction product can be switched at well by changing the rate of reagent addition. The key to this behavior is the use of coupled equilibria, in which the products of one reversible reaction act as the substrates for another. We have shown that the rate variation in the rate between irreversible and irreversible removal reactions can be used to control the chemoselection in imine oxidation. This product selection was accomplished in the absence of any enzyme or synthetic catalysts, and the only parameter changed was the rate.

txt: High-density lipoproteins (HDL) are thought to have anti-atherosclerotic properties, but recent clinical trials have failed to prove their effectiveness against atherosclerosis. ApolipoproteinE (ApoE) is a key apolipoproteins in the brain and plays a key role in cholesterol transport and homeostasis. ApoE is also a key component of the lipid-rich plasma membrane and is thought to play a role in lipid exchange. In this study, ApoA1-based recombinant high-density HDL (rHDL), Apo3- and Apo4-based rHDL (AapoE-rHDD) are synthesised and characterised using neutron reflectometry (NR) and small angle neutron scattering (SANS). The interaction of Apo1, ApoproteinA1, and Apoprotein E3 with model membranes is explored using NR. The interaction between Apo2 and Apolipid E4 is also explored using SANS. The lipid exchange capacity of ApopoE-based Apo-rH-HDL is explored by NR. In the absence of cholesterol, ApoloproteinE-containing rHDD is shown to have similar lipid exchange properties to ApoH-based HDL, but in the presence of cholesterol the protein-lipid particles are shown to be more efficient at removing cholesterol from model membranes. The ApoL-based particles are compared to Apoproto-HDD and mature HDL, and the results are compared with the results of a previous study showing that ApoHDL have similar properties to the ApoADH-containing particles.

txt: High-density lipoprotein (HDL) is a lipid-rich particle with a lipid core encased in a lipid bilayer surrounded by protein. Apolipoprotein E (ApoE) is the main apolipoproteins in the brain, where there is a local homeostasis of cholesterol. In this paper, the initial interaction of ApoE3 and Apo7 with saturated and unsaturated supported lipid bilayers (SLBs) is explored using neutron reflectometry (NR). Then, ApoEs-containing HDL (AapoE-rHDL), based on the vesicle solubilisation method often used to make ApoA1-rHDRL, are formed based on a vesicular solubility method. The Apo1-based rHDL is further characterised using small angle neutron scattering (SANS). Finally, the lipid exchange capacity for Apo-r-HDL with model membranes is explored by NR. As ApoHDRl is the most abundant apoliprotein in the human brain, the model membranes in question are in the absence or presence of cholesterol to determine the potential differences between these interactions. Comparisons are made between to ApoL-based HDL and mature HDL pooled from three healthy male volunteers [mature HDL is replotted from Waldie et al., Waldie, 2020].

txt: High-density lipoprotein (HDL) is a lipid-encapsulated protein that plays a key role in the regulation of cholesterol levels in the body. Lipid exchange is a key process in the development of atherosclerosis and Alzheimer's disease (AD), and is thought to be a potential therapeutic target for both diseases. ApolipoproteinE (ApoE) is one of the main apolipoproteins found in human HDL and plays a central role in cholesterol transport. In this study, we investigate the interaction of ApoE-containing recombinant HDL (rHDL), a form of artificial HDL, with model membranes. The interaction of the ApoA1-based Apo-rHDD with saturated and unsaturated supported lipid bilayers (SLBs) is explored using neutron reflectometry (NR). The interaction is found to be similar to that of mature HDL, but the interaction with unsaturated membranes is more complex. The lipid exchange capacity of ApOE-rHDRL is explored by NR with model lipid membranes in the absence and presence of cholesterol. The results show that Apo3 and Apo4 are able to exchange cholesterol with saturated membranes, but not unsaturated ones, with a rate similar to mature HDL. The exchange capacity is also similar to HDL, suggesting that the lipid exchange properties of ApolE-based rHDL are similar to those of HDL.

txt: Redox flow batteries (RFBs) are a promising candidate for large-scale energy storage because of the advantages of decoupled power and energy control, the minimal maintenance required, and non-flammable features in aqueous electrolytes. However, membranes separating the catholyte and anolyte are still a limiting factor for further development of next-generation RFBs. Here, graphene oxide (GO)based membranes show potential as a new class of RFB separators because of their precise size-exclusion properties, mechanical and chemical stability, and flexible functionalization. This work systematically studied the ion-transport behavior of three types of GO-based membranes by controlling hydrophilic microstructures. Because of their high ionic conductivity and precise ion selectivity, GO-breathing membranes represent a new type of low-cost yet highperformance separators for largescale energy storage systems.

txt: Graphene oxide (GO) sheets are a new class of electroactive materials with precise size exclusion properties, mechanical stability, and flexible functionalization. GO-bacteria cellulose composite membranes show potential as a new type of separators for largescale energy storage systems.

txt: Graphene oxide (GO) membranes show potential as a new class of separators for redox flow batteries because of their precise size exclusion properties, mechanical and chemical stability, and flexible functionalization. By taking advantage of the size difference between redox species and charge carriers, we propose and investigate in detail a proof-of-concept GO-based membrane for red-ox flow battery separators. The GO membrane shows high rejection of redox molecules and high ionic conductivity in aqueous solutions. Furthermore, the microstructures of GO-bacterial cellulose composite membranes can be tuned by adjusting the mass ratio of GO and the degree of oxidation of GO. Finally, we demonstrate a prototype redox-flow battery by using GO membranes as separators and utilizing riboflavin-5 0 -phosphate sodium salt and potassium ferrocyanide as redox candidates in alkaline electrolytes. The redox cell shows stable cycling with a capacity retention of >90% after 300 cycles and a Coulombic efficiency as high as 98%.

txt: The Rh-catalysed nitro-directed C–H alkynylation of nitrobenzenes is reported. The reaction tolerates a broad range of functional groups and tolerates different substituents at the ortho position. The site-selectivity is achieved by the regiodirecting effect of the nitro group, which is not dependent on the heteroarene electronics. The mechanism of the reaction is studied by experimental and computational methods. The C–N bond cleavage is shown to be the turnover limiting step, followed by alkyne insertion and bromide elimination. The regioselective alkynylation of nitrophenyl nitroarenes is also reported.

txt: The Rh-catalysed nitro-directed C–H alkynylation of nitrobenzene derivatives is an important and yet underdeveloped transformation in organic chemistry. Here we report the site-selective C–G alkynyration of nitrophenols, which tolerates a broad range of functional groups and can be performed in just four steps regioselectively from pyrene by nitration, o-alkynylations, cross-couplings, and deprotections. Our experimental and computational mechanistic investigations are consistent with a turnover limiting electrophilic C–S bond cleavage, followed by alkyne insertion and bromide elimination. We also disclose preliminary results on a related C–X iodination reaction, which may pave the way for other types of ortho-functionalization via sequential Rh/Pd catalysis.

txt: AbstractIn this study, we designed and synthesised a series of novel 3(2H)-pyridazinone derivatives. The compounds were evaluated for their cytostatic activity against the human HCT116 cell line, their toxicity in the Artemia salina lethality assay in vivo, the HCT 116 viability after serotonin challenging and compound treatment, the release of kynurenic acid after compound treatment and, lastly, the capability to limit the spontaneous migration of HCT106 cells in the wound healing paradigm. The results of the study revealed that the compounds were active against HCT-116 cells and the compounds showed a good selectivity index with respect to human fibroblasts.

txt: AbstractIn this study, fifteen novel 3(2H)-pyridazinone derivatives were synthesised and evaluated for their cytostatic activity against the human colorectal carcinoma cell line HCT116. The cytostasis of the compounds was evaluated in the Artemia salina lethality assay in vivo. The compounds VIa, VIb, VIc, VIe, VIf, VIg, VIh, VIk, VIl, VIn, VIo, VIq, VIz, VIr, VIt, VIu, VIv, VIw, VIvi, VIx, VIi, VIii, VIiv, VIix, VIir, VIus, VIvir, VIs, VIurs, VIvesi, Vitesh, Vimesh, Ziv, Vinesh, and Vimeshin were screened for their ability to induce apoptosis in HCT 116 cells. The results of the study revealed that compounds VIb and VIe exhibited the highest cytostatin activity against HCT-116 cells. In addition, compounds VIe and VIg showed the highest inhibition of the spontaneous migration of HCT–116 cells in the wound healing paradigm.

txt: AbstractIn this study, we designed fifteen new 3(2H)-pyridazinones, which were tested for their anti-proliferative effects against the human HCT116 cell line, their toxicity in the Artemia salina lethality assay in vivo, the HCT 116 viability after serotonin challenging and compound treatment, the release of kynurenic acid after compound treatment and, lastly, the capability to limit the spontaneous migration of HCT106 cells in the wound healing paradigm.ResultsWe found that the most active compound, 6-(3-fluoro-4-methoxyphenyl)-3(2-yl)acetohydrazide, was highly cytostatic and showed a good selectivity index with respect to human fibroblasts. The cytostatised cells were found to be highly responsive to the treatment of the compound. The release of Kynureniac acid after the treatment was observed.ConclusionsWe found the most interesting compound, N-benzyl-4,5-dihydro-3(6H)-dihyro-pyridine-2-carboxylic acid, to be a highly cytotoxic compound.

txt: The purification of carbon monoxide (CO) is a key step in the synthesis of commodity chemicals such as alcohols, carboxylic acids, and polycarbonates. Herein, we report a method for the reversible pressure-swing chemisorption of CO on a Ni(0) complex at room temperature via ligand substitution. This method is based on the use of a multifunctional carbene ligand with a hemi-labile coordination site, which enables the desorption/desorption sequence to proceed under reduced pressure. The use of an ionic liquid as the reaction medium enhances the desorbent efficiency, which stands in sharp contrast to the typical use of ionic liquids for the absorption of CO. This work thus provides a novel strategy for the controlled purification and long-term storage of CO, which is currently the most important feedstock for the synthesis and application of commodity chemical products.

txt: We present a study aimed at examining the effects of directed attention to taste on neural activity in the gustatory cortex. Fourteen right-handed subjects (11 women, 3 men) were given 26 s of taste stimuli (5.6 \xc3\x9710\xe2\x88\x921 M sucrose, 1.8\xc3 \xce\xbaB sodium chloride, 1\xc2\xb0 citric acid, and 2.5 mM sodium bicarbonate/25 mM potassium chloride in 0.4 ml of 0.2 ml of 1 ml of saline 0.1 ml/s solution. Taste and tasteless solutions were delivered during three different conditions: (1) taste detection, (2) passive tasting while uninformed about the taste identity, and (3) passive taste, but correctly informed about the tasteless solution. We used psychophysiological interaction (PPI) analyses to examine whether there is evidence for increased functional connectivity between regions co-activated during baseline shifts associated with attention to tasteless stimuli. We also used dynamic causal modeling (DCM) to examine the connectivity of the PPI analyses with various configurations of possible influences between these regions. We predicted a hierarchical model in which topdown influences from the attention network preferentially modulate the anterior insula and frontal operculum during directed attention.

txt: The attention network has been implicated in a variety of modalities including taste perception and spatial attention. In the present study, we examined whether the attention network modulates neural response in the gustatory cortex. Fourteen right-handed subjects (11 women, 3 men) were trained to perform a taste\xe2\x80\x93tasteless task during which they were instructed to probe a tasteless solution for taste and to make a random button response. We used psychophysiological interaction (PPI) analyses to examine whether there is evidence for increased connectivity between regions co-activated during baseline shifts associated with attention to taste. We also used dynamic causal modeling (DCM) to examine the influence of the attentional network on the anterior insula and frontal operculum. We found that the attention-induced connectivity between the gusto-responsive and non-sensory regions was greater during the DETECT condition than during the PASSIVE condition. DCM models were used to examine connectivity between these regions and to predict the topdown influences from the attention networks. DCMs showed that the top-down influences were modulated by the attention system, and that the anterior parietal cortex and frontal eye fields were preferentially modulated during DETECTtastless\xe1\x92passivetastlessness. The DCM model predicted that the same topdown effects were modulatory during PASSIVEtastameless. These results suggest that the gustoiric attention network is a heteromodal network that modulates the gustory cortex and opercular cortex.

txt: Directed attention to taste can increase sensitivity and enhance perception. In addition to enhanced responses in the sensory cortex, neuroimaging studies consistently show engagement of a large-scale heteromodal network including the posterior parietal cortex, frontal eye fields, and the anterior and posterior cingulate cortex during directed attention tasks. The aim of the present study was to use psychophysiological interaction (PPI) analyses to examine whether the attention network modulates neural response in the gustatory cortex. We compared responses to tasteless and tastantivolum stimuli in 14 right-handed subjects during three different conditions: (1) taste detection, (2) passive tasting while uninformed about the taste identity, and (3) passive tastation, but correctly informed about the identity. We found that topdown influences from the attentional network preferentially modulate the anterior insula and frontal operculum during directed perception of taste. This was confirmed by dynamic causal modeling (DCM) analysis, which showed that responses in these regions were modulated by topdown effects from the anterior parietal and frontal eye field networks. These results suggest that the attention and gustatory networks interact to modulate neural activity in the taste-responsive cortex.

txt: DNA methylation is an epigenetic event that regulates gene transcription, genetic imprinting and genome stability. Therefore, methylation status has been explored as a potential clinical biomarker for cancer classification, diagonistics, prognostics, and proposed as a chemotherapeutic target in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS). To meet this demand, various methylation methods including specific gene methylation method have been developed and applied in the aforementioned purposes. In this paper, we report a high-throughput DNA methylation assay for regional DNA methylations (RDM) level determination using a LC-MS/MS method. The assay was validated in mobile phase spiked with indicated concentration of 5mdC and constant concentration of 2-Dexoycytidine (2dC) in 50% methanol and 5 mM ammonium formate solution. The method enabled us to characterize two TSGs (HIN-1 and RASSF1A) promoter methylation changes in a primary human breast cancer cell line. This result demonstrated that our LC-ms/MS assay is effective to measure the basal level of regional DNAmethylation and its alteration induced by hypomethylating agents.

txt: A novel method for quantitative analysis of regional DNA methylation level by incorporation with bisulfite-treated PCR was developed and validated for the determination of hypomethylating activity of decitabine in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The method was applied to characterize the hypomething activity of the tumor suppressor gene (TSG) HIN-1 and the tumor suppressive gene 1A (RASSF1A) in a primary human breast cancer cell line. The method involves bisulfitization of genomic DNA to convert cytosine (C) into uracil (U), and methylation dependent sequence changes in the genomic DNA template. This results in dependency of the content of G in PCR amplicons on methylation levels and independency of the methylation of C in PCR amplification on methylations level of regional DNAs. The ratio of 5-methylcytosine-phospho-Guanosine to 2-deoxycytidine (5mdC/2dC) was used to express the DNA methylations levels. The LC-MS/MS method was validated in the range of 40 fmol to 200 pmol (1 ng/ml to 500 ng/mL) of 5mdC and 2dC. The inter-day and intra-day precision and accuracy of using the ratio of the ratio 5md/2-deoxysubstituted 5md as the indicator of regional methylation at 0.2%, 2%, 10% and 20% was found to be within the physiologic range of RGM. The assay was applied for the analysis of the promoter methylation changes induced by decitahydroimmuno-1A (HIN- 1A) and HINHIN1 (RassF1AR) in MCF-7 cells. The results demonstrated that the method is effective to measure the basal level of DNA methylating and its alteration induced by hypometomethying agents.

txt: Background: DNA methylation status has been explored as a potential clinical biomarker for cancer classification, diagonistics, prognostics, and proposed as a chemotherapeutic target in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). To meet this demand, various methylation methods including specific gene methylation techniques have been developed and applied in the aforementioned purposes. However, different quantitative high-throughput DNA methylations methods have resulted in inconsistent results. Therefore, there is a need for a screening technique that will allow for the rapid and reliable evaluation of DNA methylated and to provide quantitative information on the methylation density of the entire amplified region, not only of a few CpG loci that are covered by PCR primers. Methods: We adapted, improved and validated a recently reported LC-MS/MS method for determination of global DNA methylating level as a pharmacodynamic endpoint of hypomethylating agents. The method was applied to characterize the in-vitro and in- vivo hypometthylating activity of decitabine in AML. Results: The method enabled us to characterize two tumor suppressor gene promoters (HIN-1 and RASSF1A) promoter methylation changes in a primary human breast cancer cell line. Conclusion: Our LC- MS/MS approach is effective to measure the basal level of regional DNA methyltransferase (TSG) hypomethistylation and its alteration induced by hypometomethylethylation agents.

txt: A proof-of-concept study was conducted to determine the structural requirements for the design, synthesis, and component conjugation-site tolerance of a potentiator\xe2\x80\x93corrector linked hybrid molecule. The hybrid was synthesized from a potentiation fragment containing a benzyl alcohol and a corrector fragment containing an ethylene glycol linker. The two fragments were designed to have distinct activities in the corrector and potentiator assays. The potentiator and corrector fragments were hydrolyzed to the corresponding fragments as identified by LC/MS. The resultant potentiator-corrector hybrid was active in the correction of defective \xce\x94F508-CFTR cellular processing and chloride channel gating, respectively. This study provides proof-in-principle for the development of a multi-ligand approach for the treatment of cystic fibrosis.

txt: Cystic fibrosis is a genetic disease caused by mutations in the cystic fibrotic transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene (CFPR) that encodes a chloride channel. Mutations in \xce\x94F508-CFTR lead to distinct defects in channel gating and cellular processing. Cystic fibro-fibrosis is caused by the \xcf508-\xce"F508 mutation, which causes mutations in CFTR that lead to CFTR misfolding and endoplasmic reticulum retention, and defective channel galing. We previously identified several classes of small-molecule activators and correctors that correct each of these two defects. Herein, we report proof-of-principle data toward the design, synthesis, and component conjugation-site tolerance of a potentiator\xe2\x80\x93corrector linked hybrid molecule. This work provides proof-oftwo-principles data toward a proof-o-prine approach to the design and synthesis of a CFTR potentiator-corrector hybrid.

txt: Cystic fibrosis is a genetic disease caused by mutations in the cystic fibrotic transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene (CFPR) that encodes a chloride channel. Mutations in \xce\x94F508-CFTR lead to distinct defects in channel gating and cellular processing. Small-molecule therapies for cystic cystic Fibrosis will likely require compounds that correct the two major underlying defects in CFTR: a) CFTR misfolding and endoplasmic reticulum retention, and b) defective channel gated channel gates. Herein, we report proof-of-principle data for the design, synthesis, and component conjugation-site tolerance of a potentiator\xe2\x80\x93corrector linked hybrid molecule. The hybrid was synthesized from a potentiator and a corrector fragment linked by a linker. The resultant potentiator and corrector fragments following hydrolysis, as would occur in the gastrointestinal tract, were active in the correction of defective \xcf\x89F508 CFTR cellular processing and chloride channel gagging, respectively. This work provides proof-for-concept for the development of a single compound that can confer distinct activities required to restore chloride channel function in cystic-fibrosis caused by the \xf\x88F508 mutation.

txt: In this study, a method was developed for the determination of endogenous signal compounds in U. pumila leaves infected with Tetraneura akinire Sasaki. The aim of this study was to reveal change trends of endogenous jasmonic acid and salicylic acid levels in host U.pumila leaf infected with the aphid (Tetraneura odatus). The method was based on extraction, purification, and GC-MS determination. The extraction and purification conditions were optimized using ethyl acetate and n-hexane as extract solvent and dihydrojasmonate as an extract standard. The chromatographic separation was performed using DB-5 column (30 m × 0.25 mm × 0.25 μm) with a helium flow rate of 1.1 mL/min. The selected ion monitoring (SIM) mode was used for quantification after electron ionization (70 eV) with dwell time set at 0.3 s, and source temperature and quadrupole temperature were set at 230°C and 150°C, respectively. The mass data were collected in the range from m/z 40 to m/Z 500. The method showed good linearity (r 2 = 0.9976) and limit of detection (LOD = 0,000.00 μg/mg) and limits of quantification (LOQ = 0 μg/g) with good precision (RSD = 2.14% to 11.05%). The method can be used for the quantification of these endogenous compounds in host plants.

txt: A simple, rapid, and sensitive GC-MS method was established for the determination of endogenous signal compounds in Ulmus pumila leaves. The extraction and purification methods of four signal compounds, jasmonic acid, salicylic acid, methyl salicylate, methyl jasmanate, and dihydrojasmonate, were optimized. The chromatographic separation was achieved using DB-5 column (30 m × 0.25 mm × 0, 25 μm) with helium flow rate of 1.1 mL/min. The injection temperature and injected volume were set to 280°C and 2 μL, respectively. The selected ion monitoring (SIM) mode was used for the quantification of the signal compounds. The method showed good linearity (r 2 > 0.9997) and precision (intraday and interday precision < 4.02%). The recoveries of the four signal compound were in the range of 73.8%–103.0%, and the RSD values were less than 11.05%. The method was successfully applied for the analysis of U. pumilai gall formation stage, growth, and dehiscence. The results showed that salicyclic acid and jasmoronic acid levels were significantly higher in the early stage of infection, then reached their peak (up to 24-fold higher) compared to the control, and then decreased. In addition, methylsalicylates level was significantly higher than the control at early stage, then gradually increased to the highest (up 2.9-fold) in the middle stage, and finally decreased.

txt: We report a straightforward synthesis of a family of P-containing acenaphthylenes and phenanthrenes featuring internal ylidic bond. These compounds are easily obtained through intramolecular cyclization of readily available phosphine ylides generated from bromo-naphthoyl phosphine. The molecular engineering of this heterocycle allows tuning their photophysical properties as well as their redox properties. The method is fully compatible for the efficient preparation of linear and chiral P-based acenes and helicenes. Furthermore, we could also endow them with chiroptical or non-linear optical properties.

txt: In this article, a family of organophosphorus -conjugated heterocycles featuring internal ylidic bond was prepared via a straightforward synthesis that allows obtaining in one-pot P-containing acenes or phenanthrenes featuring internal Ylidics bond. These compounds are easily obtained through intramolecular cyclization of carbonyl-stabilized phosphonium ylides generated from readily available phosphine D and F. The method is fully compatible for the efficient preparation of more elaborated P-heterocycles such as  5 -phosphaphenanthrene and  5 -dithienophosphinine. The molecular engineering of this heterocycle allows tuning their photophysical properties as well as their redox properties. These modifications were rationalized using DFT methods. Finally, we could also endow them with chiroptical or non-linear optical properties.

txt: Lithium metal is one of the most promising anode materials for the next-generation lithium-ion batteries. However, the interface instability between the lithium metal anode and solid-state electrolyte (SSE) is a major obstacle for the practical application of lithium metal-based batteries. Herein, we report a new strategy to solve this interfacial issue by using an in situ “welding” strategy. The interface between the anode lithium metal and the solid-states electrolyte is wetted by microliter-level of liquid electrolyte during cell assembling, which is transformed into an organic-inorganic composite buffer layer. The soft organic component connects the lithium anode with the solid state electrolytes, buffers the volume change of the lithium metals during the assembling process, eliminates solid–solid point contact and ensures a regulated Li+ flow on the interface, while the inorganic component demonstrates much better electrochemical stability offering a flexible and stable interface and promoting enhanced electrochemical performance. Symmetric lithium–metal batteries with the new interface demonstrate good cycling performance for 400 h and withstand the current density of 0.4 mA cm−2. Full batteries developed with lithium– metal anodes and LiFePO4 cathode also demonstrate significantly improved cycling endurance and capacity retention.

txt: Lithium metal is one of the most promising candidates for the next-generation battery. However, it is hard to form a stable and dense SEI layer on the lithium metal anodes of cells with liquid electrolytes due to the continuous reactions between lithium metal and the liquid electrolyte due to continuous reactions. In this work, the interfacial issue in solid-state batteries is addressed by an in situ “welding” strategy. Specifically, the interface between anode and the solid-states electrolyte is wetted by microliter-level of liquid electrolyite during cell assembling, which is transformed into an organic-inorganic composite buffer layer. In the in situ solidified layer, the soft organic component connects the lithium anode with the solid state electrolytes, buffers the volume change of the lithiummetal anode during the plating/stripping process, eliminates solid–solid point contact and ensures a regulated Li+ flow on the interface; meanwhile, the inorganic component demonstrates much better electrochemical stability offering a flexible and stable interface and promoting enhanced electrochemical performance. Symmetric lithium–metal batteries with the new interface demonstrate good cycling performance for 400 h and withstand the current density of 0.4 mA cm−2. Full batteries developed with lithium–Metal anode (LiFePO4 cathode) and Li2OHX (X = Cl, Br, I) electrolytes also demonstrate significantly improved cycling endurance and capacity retention.

txt: Lithium metal anode materials have been reported as one of the most promising candidates for the next-generation battery. However, the interface instability between the lithium metal anodes and solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) is a major obstacle to the practical application of lithium metal-based anodes. In this work, an in situ solidified interface is developed to address the interface stability of lithium–metal anodes in solid-ion batteries. The interface between the anode and the solid-structure electrolyte is wetted by microliter-level of liquid electrolyte during cell assembling, which is transformed into an organic-inorganic composite buffer layer. The soft organic component connects the lithium anode with the solid state electrolyte, buffers the volume change of the lithium–solid point contact, eliminates solid–solid contact and ensures a regulated Li+ flow on the interface, while the inorganic component provides much better electrochemical stability. The new interface provides a flexible and stable interface and promotes enhanced electrochemical performance. Symmetric lithium– metal batteries with the new interface demonstrate good cycling performance for 400 h and withstand the current density of 0.4 mA cm−2. Full batteries developed with lithium–Metal anode (LiFePO4 cathode) and Li2OHCl anode also demonstrate significantly improved cycling endurance and capacity retention.

txt: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous malignancy characterized by the accumulation of transformed myeloids resulting in impaired production of red blood cells, neutrophils, and platelets as well as diminished immune function. Relapse results from the inability of chemotherapeutics to eliminate the AML cells residing in the bone marrow that give rise to further disease. Understanding how to effectively target AML stem cells within the bone bone marrow microenvironment is crucial to eliminating the resident AML leukemic stem cells responsible for relapse. We recently demonstrated that SDF-1, the sole endogenous ligand for the CXCR4 chemokine receptor, induces apoptosis ex vivo in AML cell lines and patient samples that express elevated levels of cell-surface CXC4. However, AML can survive and grow in the endosteal niche, a protective bone-proximal niche within the marrow microenvironments that attracts and supports the survival and maintenance of the pluripotent hematopoietic stem cells (HSC) that give give rise various blood cell lineages. The endosteum is composed of many cell types, including mesenchymal stem cells, stromal cells, osteoprogenitors, osteoblasts, and osteoclasts, but the identity of the cells that protect and nurture HSC and/or AML patients is unclear. Here, we utilized co-culture systems to identify which cells within bone marrow cells that could protect AML from SDF1-induced apoptosis. We found that mesenchyme/stem cells, but not osteoblastic cells, were capable of protecting AML-expressing cells from SGF-1-dependent apoptosis in co-cultures. Moreover, osteoblast-lineage cells, including osteocalcin-producing osteoblast cells, mesenchylangiopoietin-producing stroma, osteoclastic cells and osteopontin-1 cells, and bone marrow-derived mesenchysmal stromals, were able to protect AMC-1 and osteoblasts from Sdf-1 induced apoptosis, but osteoclast cells were unable to protect osteoblaster-lineages from SDCF-1. Our results indicate that differentiating osteobllast cells play a crucial role in protecting AMC cell survival in the marrow endostal niche.

Relapse results from the inability of chemotherapeutics to eliminate AML cells residing in the bone marrow that give rise to further disease. Understanding how to effectively target AML stem cells within the bone-proximal niche is crucial to eliminating the resident AML leukemic stem cells responsible for relapse. We recently demonstrated that SDF-1, which is the sole endogenous ligand for the CXCR4 chemokine receptor, robustly induces apoptosis in AML cell lines and patient samples expressing CXC-4 on the cell surface. SDF1 is abundant in the endosteal niche, or endosteum, which protects and nurtures the survival and growth of the pluripotent hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) that give birth to various blood cell lineages. The endostal cells are composed of mesenchymal cells, osteoblasts, osteoprogenitors, osteoclasts, and osteocalcin. We hypothesized that one or more cell types within the endostereal niche could protect AML-lineage cells from SDF(1)-induced apoptosis. To test this hypothesis, we cultured murine primary AML lines expressing elevated levels of CXR4 and differentiating osteoblastic cells in co-culture with different cell types found in the osteoblast lineage. We found that osteoblast cells, but not mesenchyme cells, were capable of protecting AML lineages from SGF-1-induced apoptotic cell death. Moreover, osteocalin-producing osteoblact cells, which are abundant in bone marrow, were unable to protect AMM cells from apoptosis induced by SDF-(1)-dependent apoptosis of osteoblaut cells. Our results indicate that differentiating mesenchylal cells within bone marrow play a crucial role in protecting AMM stem cells from the SDF\xe2\x80\x931-dependent apoptotic pathway.

txt: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous malignancy characterized by the accumulation of transformed myeloids resulting in impaired production of red blood cells, neutrophils, and platelets as well as diminished immune function. Understanding how to effectively target AML cells within the bone marrow microenvironment is crucial to eliminating the resident AML leukemic stem cells responsible for relapse. We recently demonstrated that SDF-1 (also known as CXCL12), which is the sole endogenous ligand for the CXCR4 chemokine receptor, robustly induces apoptotic cell death through the intrinsic pathway in AML cell lines and a significant fraction of patient samples expressing CXC4 on the cell surface. We previously demonstrated that mesenchymal stromal/stem cells can promote AML cancer cell survival via regulation of Bcl-2 and acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) cell survival through the Notch pathway. We therefore hypothesized that one or more cell types within the marrow micro-environment has the ability to tonically inhibit the SDF1-driven apoptotic pathway in the bone-proximal niche of the bone. Here, we utilized co-culture systems to identify which cells of the osteoblast lineage have the capacity to protect CXR4-expressing AML stem cells from SDF(1) cell death. Our results indicate that differentiating osteoblasts play a crucial role in protecting AML-stem cells from apoptosis induced by SDF[1] cell death in the endosteal niches of the marrow.

txt: We present a benchmark set for charge transfer (CT) states of two-component molecular complexes. The benchmark set consists of local and CT type states of the tetrafluoroethylene-ethylene and ammoniafluorine-fluoride complexes, as well as of the pyrrole-pyrazine-pyrrole and pyrrolidine-piperazine-pyrimidine-pyazine complexes. In this set, the CCSD level approximation to Equation-of-Motion Coupled-Cluster Singles and Doubles (CCSD) is used as a reference. The CCSDT-3 and CCS-CCSD(T) methods are used for the smaller systems, while the iterative CCSdt-3 is used for larger systems. The performance of different methods is evaluated as a function of the excitation energy, the energy ordering of the states, and the energy of the lowest state. The results obtained are compared to the reference values obtained with the CCD-CC2 and CCD(T)-CCSD methods. The accuracy of the methods is compared to that of the CCCSD-LR method. The comparison of the results obtained with different methods reveals that the CCT-CCS-3 method is more accurate than the Cccssd-LR variant, while CCSd-T is more reliable than CCSDSD-LR.

txt: Charge transfer (CT) states are special types of electronically excited states, which are of key importance in processes related to molecular conductance and electron transfer properties. As these states tend to show up in larger molecules and complexes, approximate theoretical methods need to be invoked for their description. The popular time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) is, however, known to underestimate considerably the excitation energies of CT states, at least with standard functionals. Therefore, there is a demand for wave function methods which are economic enough to treat large systems of chemical interest, or at least can provide reliable benchmark results to test and calibrate other methods. In this study, we aim at establishing a benchmark set from local and CT type states of two-component molecular complexes by providing high level (CCSDT and CCSDT-3) benchmark values. This benchmark set is then used to characterize the reliability of various methods of the Coupled-Cluster hierarchy for charge transfer excitation energy calculations. In the present study, the performance of different methods has been systematically examined for CT states. In order to test quantum chemical methods, we have included several program systems, e.g. CC2, CCSD, CCA, CC3, CC2-CC2, CC4, CC5, CCC6, Cccc-CC6-CC5, CC6-Ccc-CC7, Cccc-Cc-Cd-CC8, Ccsd-Ccsd, Cx-CCd-3, Ccl-CCc-ccc, Cct-CCx, Ct-CCt, Cxt-CCl, Cnt-CCcl, Cmt-CCm, Cpt-CCr-CCs, Ctm-CCcsd and Cmtc-CTr-Cm. The results of the benchmark studies are presented.

txt: We present a benchmark set for the description of charge transfer (CT) states of two-component molecular complexes. The set consists of 41 CT states of the tetrafluoroethylene-ethylene and pyrrole-pyrazine systems, with the CCSD level approximation (CCSDT and CCSDT-3) as the reference. The performance of several approximate triples methods (CC2, ADC(2), CC3 and EOM-CCSD) is compared with the reference CCSDPT method. The CT states are identified and characterized using the natural orbitals of the difference density and numerical descriptors of the ground and excited states, as well as the one-particle transition density. The results show that the C2 and ADC(3) methods are able to describe the CT states with reasonable accuracy, while the CCCSD-3 and COSMOS-CC2 methods are found to be less accurate. The CCSDs are found not to be able to provide reliable benchmarks for the CT type states of tetraflamine-fluorine and pryrole- pyrazine complexes.

txt: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is an endogenous gasotransmitter produced by mammalian cells. It is known to regulate a variety of physiological and pathophysiological processes in health and disease. Mice deficient in cystathionine gamma-lyase (CSE), the major H2S-producing enzyme, exhibit exacerbated pathophysiology, underlying the protective role of endogenously produced H2s in the regulation of various biological processes. The current article reports on our findings in CSE-deficient mice showing that the mice exhibit significant hematological changes compared to the wild-type animals. When exploring the underlying mechanisms, we have identified the upregulation of coproporphyrinogen oxidase (CPOX), a key enzyme in heme biosynthesis \xe2\x80\x93 in C-type mice. Because porphyrins are key components of heme synthesis and erythropoiesis, and also of mitochondrial electron transport chain proteins, we explored the potential importance of CSE\xe2 \x88\x92/\xe22\x88\'s CPOX in two aspects of metabolism: (a) oxygen transport and global hypoxia resistance and (b) mitochondrial electron transporting and cellular bioenergetics. We found that CSE is upregulated in the liver of C-types mice, and that CPOE is also upregulated. In addition, we found that the CSE upregulated CPOEs are upregulated by siRNA-mediated silencing. We also found that in addition to the C-C motif, CSE also upregulates the levels of CPOES in liver mitochondria. In summary, our results suggest that C-based approaches to CSE and CPOe silencing may be useful in the treatment of COS-related diseases.

txt: Mice deficient in cystathionine gamma-lyase (CSE) are known to have a protective role in the regulation of cardiovascular and neurological functions. However, there are also some conditions where CSE deficiency was found to confer protection. The current article reports on our findings in CSE-deficient mice showing that the mice exhibit significant hematological changes compared to the wild-type animals. When exploring the underlying mechanisms, we have identified the upregulation of coproporphyrinogen oxidase (CPOX), a key enzyme in heme biosynthesis, in Cse\xe2\x88\x92/\xe22\x80\x93 mice. Because porphyrins are produced by CSE, and CPOX has an important role not only in hemes synthesis and erythropoiesis, but also in the production of mitochondrial electron transport chain proteins, we explored the potential importance of CSE\xe1\x89\xabregulated CPOx in two aspects of metabolism: (a) oxygen transport and global hypoxia resistance and (b) mitochondrial electron transporting and cellular bioenergetics. We found that CSE is upregulated in C\xe21\xce\xb2-catenin-dependent and C\xcf\x83-catenzymes, and that C\xc2\xb7xH2O, a CSE inhibitor, is required for CSE activity. CSE and CpoX are also upregulated when CSE was inhibited by the CSE/CSE inhibitor DL-propargylglycine. C\xb1-catensin-independent CSE isoforms were also up-regulated in liver mitochondria. CSPOx was also upregulated in liver tissue samples from CSE \xe2 \xce \xb2\xe80\xb3-catalysed CSE knockout mice. CPOox was also increased in liver homogenates of CSPOs\xe3\xaf\xac\x8b and wild-types. COS-dependent CSPoX was also found in liver tissues of Cse- and CSE -KO mice. These results suggest that CSPos is up-regulated when Cse is inhibited in CSPOS\xe23\xf\x86\x87\x82/\x84 mice, and suggest that the up-regulation of CspoX is important in maintaining CSE function and in maintaining mitochondrial electron homeostasis.

txt: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is an endogenous gasotransmitter produced by mammalian cells. It is known to regulate a variety of physiological and pathophysiological processes in health and disease. Mice deficient in cystathionine gamma-lyase (CSE) have been generated (global knockouts) with some baseline alterations, suggesting the importance of endogenously produced H2S in the regulation of cardiovascular and neurological functions. In addition, in several disease models, mice that are deficient in H2sulfide-producing enzymes exhibit exacerbated pathophysiologic responses, underlying the protective role of endogenous produced H 2S in regulation of various biological processes. The current article reports on our findings in CSE-deficient mice showing that the mice exhibit significant hematological changes compared to the wild-type animals. When exploring the underlying mechanisms, we have identified the upregulation of coproporphyrinogen oxidase (CPOX) \xe2\x80\x93 a key enzyme in heme biosynthesis \xe3\x88\x92/\xe2" in Cse\xe3"/\x935\xe1\x8b mice. Because porphyrins are key intermediates in hemes biosynthesis, catalyzed by CPOX, have an important role not only in heem synthesis and erythropoiesis, but also in the production of mitochondrial electron transport chain proteins, we explored the potential importance of CSEregulated CPOx in two aspects of metabolism: (a) oxygen transport and global hypoxia resistance and (b) mitochondrial electron-transport and cellular bioenergetics.

txt: A novel, efficient Turkish perlite supported nickel oxide catalyst (NPC-15) was prepared by loading nickel oxide on thermally activated Turkish perlitic perlite (TAP) by deposition-precipitation method, using NaOH as a basification agent. The required amounts (1.97 g for 10 wt. %, 2.95 g for 15 wt., 9.83 g for 50 wt..) of precursor salt (nickel nitrate) in an aqueous solution phase were mixed with 5 g of TAP and agitated for 12 h at room temperature. The catalytic performance of NPC-15 was tested for a series of Claisen–Schmidt condensation reactions, which is quite an uncommon field of catalysis for supported nickel oxides. Use of less expensive support, recyclable catalyst, solvent-less reaction conditions, green methodology, ease of product purification are the key features of this protocol, and, thus, it may be considered as an efficient alternative to the existing, high-priced, less-effective procedures. This work is aimed to act as a stepping-stone for the prospective researchers into the rewarding field of utilization of waste materials like Turkish perlate as the catalyst support in the development of heterogeneous catalysts.

txt: A novel, efficient Turkish perlite supported nickel oxide catalyst (NPC-15) was prepared by loading nickel oxide on thermally activated Turkish perlitic acid (TAP) by deposition-precipitation method, using NaOH as a basification agent. The catalyst was characterized by BET surface area analysis, XRD, SEM, SEM-EDX JEOL, TEM, FT-IR, pyridine adsorbed FT- IR, UV-Vis DRS, and TGA techniques. The catalytic performance of NPC-15 was tested for a series of Claisen–Schmidt condensation reactions, giving a higher isolated yield % of desired products, 2,6-bis(substituted benzylidene)cyclohexanone, used in anti-tumor, anti-cancer, and cytotoxic activities. The results indicate that the particle size of NPC‒15 is less than 50 nm. The particle size is also less than 20 times smaller than that of NPC in TAP. The present protocol is eco-friendly, eco-compatible, and eco-stable, and recyclable, and can be used for up to six consecutive reaction cycles.

txt: A novel, efficient Turkish perlite supported nickel oxide catalyst (NPC-15) was prepared by loading nickel oxide on thermally activated Turkish perlites (TAP) by deposition-precipitation method, using NaOH as a basification agent. The catalytic performance of NPC-15 was evaluated by a series of Claisen–Schmidt condensation reactions. The results show that NPC-10, 15, and 50 catalysts exhibited higher isolated yields of desired products, 2,6-bis(substituted benzylidene)cyclohexanone and 2,7-bis-bis-(substituents) cyclohexane, respectively, than Turkish per-lite (TPL) and commercial nickel oxide (NiO). The catalysts were characterized by BET surface area analysis, XRD, SEM, SEM-EDX, TEM, FT-IR, and TGA. The presence of nickel oxide in all catalysts confirmed its effective loading on the Turkish perite surface. The catalyst was found to be recyclable up to six consecutive reaction cycles.

txt: The extracellular flux (XF) instrument is a plate-based assay for measuring mitochondrial biogenesis in primary cultures of the rabbit renal tubular epithelial cells (RPTC). The XF-24 instrument was optimized for the Seahorse Biosciences extraceventilatory flux (RTPTC) platform and tested for its ability to measure mitochondrial biogenic activity. The XFs were used to measure oxygen consumption rates (OCR) in RPTC cultured under optimized conditions (shaking, with lactate and no glucose) and in the presence of oligomycin, an inhibitor of the F1F0-ATPase, to determine the fraction of the OCR that is coupled to maintenance of plasma membrane potential. FCCP uncoupled the mitochondrial membrane potential to increase the Ocrase capacity. The AMP-kinase activator aminoimidazole carboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) increased FCCP OCR at 300 and 500 \xce\xbcM and basal Ocras increased at 500 \xc2\xb1 500 \xe2\x88\x921 with a maximal increase of approximately 40% (Fig. 1A). Metformin, a biguanide anti-diabetic drug, increased basal and uncouplated Ocrases to a similar extent as AICAR. The piperazine-thiazole SRT1720 was also shown to induce mitochondrial biogenesis. The 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) receptor agonist 1-(2,5-dimethoxy-4-iodophenyl)-2-aminopropane hydrochloride (DOI) increased basal OCR by 40% in RPtc cultured under standard conditions. Similarly, treatment of RPTC with resveratrol or the isoflavone daidzein (10 \xcf\x83M) increased both basal and uncoupled OcrAs by ~40% (Rs = 0.5-0.5). The results demonstrate that the XF instrument is an ideal model to measure the loss of mitochondrial function in RPTricular epithelia and could be used to assess nephrotoxic liability of new chemicals, environmental agents, and consumer products.

txt: Mitochondria are the primary site of mitochondrial biogenesis in the kidney. The kidneys are the most susceptible organ to nephrotoxicants and many drugs and environmental agents. The renal tubular epithelia (RPTC) are capable of mitochondrial respiration and have a capacity for repair and regeneration. We recently demonstrated that RPTC can produce mitochondrial biogenic agents that induce mitochondrial biogenetic processes. To assess the potential of the XF-24 instrument to measure mitochondrial biogeneration, primary RPTC were cultured under optimized conditions, treated with several nephrophrotoxicant agents, and the uncoupled oxygen consumption rate (OCR) was measured. The results show that the X-F- 24 instrument is a sensitive, functional assay of mitochondrial damage. The XF instrument provides a sensitive measure of nephro-toxicity prior to onset of cell death.

txt: Mitochondria are the primary targets of many drugs, environmental chemicals, and drugs for xenobiotics. The loss of mitochondrial respiratory capacity is a hallmark of many nephrotoxicants and is a particular problem in those cells/tissues that primarily rely on aerobic metabolism (e.g. kidney). The loss in mitochondrial respiratory function is a phenotypic stress response and is likely more physiological that a single pathway readout given that these cells retain function that is metabolically coupled. We recently demonstrated that several classes of compounds produce mitochondrial biogenesis in the renal tubular epithelia (RPTC) and that FCCP-uncoupled oxygen consumption rate (OCR) is a marker of mitochondrial biogenic activity. To assess the potential of a respirometric assay to measure the loss of respiratory capacity in RPTC, the primary culture of RPTC was optimized for the Seahorse Biosciences extracellular flux (XF) analyzer and tested with several nephroprotoxicants. The XF-24 instrument was able to measure both basal and uncoupled OCR rates in RP TC cultured under optimized conditions. The uncoupling of OCR was also found to be a sensitive measure of mitochondrial damage in RPT cells treated with several classes known to produce mitochondrial damage. The results demonstrate that the XF instrument provides a sensitive, functional assay of mitochondrial dysfunction that can be used to assess the nephrophrotoxicity potential of new chemicals, environmental agents, and consumer products.

txt: We present a set of atom-centered potentials (ACPs) designed to improve the accuracy of the HF-3c method for non-covalent interactions and molecular structures. The ACPs are developed for a larger set of atoms (H, B, C, N, O, F, Si, P, S, and Cl) than in our previous work, greatly increasing the applicability of the proposed methods. The LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) regression is used to carry out the fitting of the ACP parameters, resulting in more robust and more widely applicable methods. Three of the four new ACP-corrected methods are based on HF with minimal (MINIs 82 and MINIX 37 ) or small double-ζ basis sets (6-31G* 83, 84 ) and use Grimme's D3 correction to account for the missing dispersion in HF. In addition, we also present a new ACPs designed to increase the accuracy and cost of the corresponding HF-based methods. In all cases, the target applications are similar to those of HF- 3c and our previous study, namely structures and non-bonding interaction strengths. However, the ACPs developed for H, B and C atoms are developed using a larger training set than in the previous work. The new ACPS are assessed using an extensive validation set, demonstrating their performance and robustness.

txt: We present four atom-centered potentials (ACPs) designed to improve the accuracy of the HF-3c method for non-covalent interactions. The ACP-corrected methods are based on HF with minimal (MINIs 82 and MINIX 37 ) or small double-ζ basis sets (6-31G* 83,84 ) and use Grimme's D3 correction to account for the missing dispersion in HF. In addition, we also present a set of ACPs designed to further improve the performance of the existing HF-based methods. The training set used here is much larger than in our previous work (73832 data points, 167275 molecular geometries, and 10288 molecular deformation energies) and contains representative candidates from the interaction types hydrogen bonding, conformational energies, and molecular conformational energy. The new ACP methods are assessed using an extensive validation set, demonstrating their performance and robustness. The results show that the new ACPs are able to accurately predict the non-bonding interaction strengths of the training set and the conformational and deformation energy of the validation set. In particular, the training and validation sets show good agreement in the hydrogen bonding strength and conformational strength, with the training sets showing the highest accuracy and the validation sets showing good agreement with the reference data. The accuracy of these training sets is also comparable to the accuracy obtained from density functional theory (DFT) based methods.

txt: We present four new methods for modeling non-covalent interaction strengths and molecular structures based on the Hartree-Fock (HF) method. The methods are based on atom-centered potentials (ACPs) developed for dispersion-corrected minimal basis set HF with minimal (MINIs 82 and MINIX 37 ) or small double-ζ basis sets (6-31G* 83,84 ) and use Grimme’s D3 38,85,86 correction to account for the missing dispersion in HF. In addition, we also present a set of ACPs designed to improve the performance of the HF-3c method. In order to overcome the limitation imposed by the fact that ACPs are available only for the ten elements mentioned above, we expect HF- 3c parameters to reduce to HF-1c performance for the atoms for which ACPs have not been developed, which in general should be in the minority. The newly developed ACP-corrects are assessed using an extensive validation set, demonstrating their performance and robustness.
